title: ZDX at a glance: what it measures and which subject answers each question

prose.text: ZDX is the Zscaler product that observes user experience; this subject says what it measures and links the subject for each question. {{monitors}} {{measurement-areas}} {{device-health-metrics}} {{triage-scope}}

prose.label: Setting it up.
prose.text: {{setup-order}} {{selective-entitlement}} The minimum Client Connector and ZDX Module versions are in [[zdx.compatibility.supported-versions]].

prose.label: Architecture.
prose.text: {{module-architecture}} {{platforms-and-probe-types}} The components and the path telemetry takes are in [[zdx.cloud-architecture]], and ZDX Module releases and rollouts on Client Connector are in [[zdx.cloud-architecture.module-upgrades]].

prose.label: Score.
prose.text: What the score and its bands mean, and the score types, are in [[zdx.score]]; how it rolls up per application, place, organization and user is in [[zdx.score.calculation]].

prose.label: Probes.
prose.text: Web and Cloud Path probes and what each measures are in [[zdx.probes]], which users a probe runs for is in [[zdx.probes.criteria]], how end-user probes are configured is in [[zdx.probes.configuration]], and how applications and their probes are grouped into collections is in [[zdx.probes.collections]].

prose.label: Applications and devices.
prose.text: Predefined, custom and network applications and the application reads are in [[zdx.applications]], and onboarding Microsoft Teams, Webex and Zoom Call Quality tenants is in [[zdx.applications.uc-tenants]]. Device lists and details are in [[zdx.devices]], with health metrics and events in [[zdx.devices.health-and-events]], geolocations in [[zdx.devices.geolocation]] and call quality in [[zdx.devices.call-quality]].

prose.label: Reading data through the API.
prose.text: Time ranges, paging and the user reads are in [[zdx.reports]], and the department and location lookups are in [[zdx.administration]]. Sign-in, rate limits and the SDKs are in [[zdx.api]] and [[zdx.sdk-python]].

prose.label: Diagnostics and alerts.
prose.text: Diagnostics Sessions, which the API calls deep traces ([[shared.terminology.product-names:zdx-deep-trace]]), are in [[zdx.diagnostics]], and alerts are in [[zdx.alerts]]; configuring alert rules, templates and labels is in [[zdx.alerts.rules]], webhooks are in [[zdx.alerts.webhooks]] and the ZDX application on ServiceNow is in [[zdx.alerts.servicenow]].

prose.label: Administration.
prose.text: ZDX admin roles, permissions, obfuscation and scope are in [[shared.admin-rbac.zdx]], and the console's admin audit log is in [[zdx.audit-logs]].

prose.label: Who reports data.
prose.text: Which users and devices run ZDX at all is set by the Client Connector entitlement, [[zcc.entitlements.zdx]]. Location collection is a separate User Privacy switch, [[zcc.web-privacy.collection:zdx-location]], and whether both are needed is open, [[zcc.entitlements.zdx:location-both-required]].

prose.label: Console dashboards.
prose.text: The Digital Experience dashboard, the Performance Dashboard, the Applications and Users Overviews, VIP tagging and Self Service are in [[zdx.dashboards]], and so is the ZIA Private Service Edge Health dashboard, which is documented in the ZDX help; whether it covers Virtual Service Edges is open {{gap:pse-dashboard}}.

prose.label: Remediation.
prose.text: Remote scripts run on devices, their jobs and their errors are in [[zdx.remediation]].

checks.do: Whether the user or device is entitled to ZDX before treating missing data as a ZDX fault.

Read a ZDX question as one about measured experience (the score, probe metrics, Cloud Path hops, a Diagnostics Session), and take the question of which policy applied to the same traffic to the product that enforces it.

monitors.statement: ZDX monitors the cloud application experience from the end-user perspective, with application performance monitoring for customer-defined applications and for predefined ones such as Zoom, Box, Salesforce, ServiceNow and the Microsoft 365 applications, including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business and Outlook.

quotes: organizations can fully monitor the cloud application experience simply and intuitively from the end user perspective

ZDX provides application performance monitoring for customer-defined applications and predefined applications such as Zoom, Box, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft 365 applications, including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, and Outlook.

measurement-areas.statement: The architecture page groups what ZDX measures into end-user device performance (resource utilization, health metrics and events such as CPU and memory use, including Wi-Fi connectivity issues), Cloud Path performance (hop-by-hop network path metrics from every user device to the application), application performance (response time, DNS resolution and availability) and the ZDX Score, an aggregated score tracked over time at the user, application, location, department and organizational level.

quotes:
End User Device Performance
- The service continuously gathers and analyzes data on end user devices, resource utilization, health metrics, and multiple events such as CPU and memory usage, including Wi-Fi connectivity issues

Cloud Path Performance
- Hop-by-hop network path metrics are measured and analyzed from end-to-end over time, from every user device to the application.

Application Performance
- ZDX continuously monitors and measures application metrics such as response time and DNS resolution, as well as broader availability metrics of the application.

ZDX Scoring
- An aggregated user experience performance score is tracked over time at the user, application, location, department, and organizational level. The ZDX Score ranks user performance

module-architecture.statement: ZDX is a multi-tenant cloud monitoring platform whose synthetic probing runs through Client Connector; ZDX support is natively integrated within Client Connector as a standalone lightweight module upgraded independently of the Client Connector core process.

quotes: ZDX support is natively integrated within Zscaler Client Connector,
The Digital Experience (ZDX) service is built as a multi-tenant, cloud-based monitoring platform
ZDX relies on the Zscaler Client Connector to perform synthetic probing
runs as a standalone lightweight module that is upgraded independently of the Zscaler Client Connector core process.

platforms-and-probe-types.statement: ZDX is implemented through Client Connector on Windows, macOS, Android, Android on ChromeOS and iOS; to monitor general data center information and key SaaS applications, the overview names HTTP, ICMP or UDP synthetic probes running on user devices.

quotes: Use Zscaler’s unified client, Zscaler Client Connector, to implement ZDX on Windows, macOS, Android, Android on ChromeOS, and iOS devices.
Monitor general data center information and your key SaaS applications
using HTTP, ICMP, or UDP synthetic probes running on user devices in near real time.

device-health-metrics.statement: ZDX collects real-time device health information such as CPU usage, memory usage, Network IO, Disk IO and Wi-Fi signal strength; the article gives these as examples.

quotes: Collect real-time device health information (i.e., CPU usage, memory usage, Network IO, Disk IO, Wi-Fi signal strength, etc.) for your user devices.

triage-scope.statement: The documented triage scope of ZDX is whether an issue is in the local network, a user's device, the ISP provider or the Zscaler cloud; remote troubleshooting capabilities include system process-level monitoring, full network path information including ASN, ISP and country hop information, and packet tracing.

quotes: Remote troubleshooting capabilities to perform detailed analyses of problematic devices
pinpoint whether the issue is in the local network, a user's device, the ISP provider, or within the Zscaler cloud.
system process-level monitoring, full network path information including the Autonomous System Number (ASN), ISP information, country hop information, and packet tracing

setup-order.statement: The ZDX step-by-step guide orders setup as: authentication and provisioning in Internet & SaaS, role-based administration, allowlisting domains on the Zscaler cloud, Client Connector configuration, applications, probes, alerting, then diagnostics; Step 1 says to have users, authentication and provisioning set up in Internet & SaaS and to contact Zscaler Support if they cannot be configured in ZIA.

quotes: Step 1: Configure Authentication and Provisioning Settings in Internet & SaaS
To configure ZDX, have users, authentication, and provisioning set up for your organization in Internet & SaaS.
If you cannot configure these settings in ZIA, contact Zscaler Support.
Step 2: Configure Role-Based Administration
Step 3: Allowlist Domains on Zscaler cloud
Step 4: Configure Zscaler Client Connector for ZDX
Step 5: Configure an Application
Step 6: Configure a Probe
Step 7: Configure Alerting

selective-entitlement.statement: After Client Connector is configured, ZDX can also be enabled for a select group of users (Selective Entitlement).

quotes: After you configure Zscaler Client Connector for your organization, you can also enable ZDX for a select group of users.
Selective Entitlement: Enabling ZDX for a Group of Users

pse-dashboard.title: Whether a separate Private Service Edge dashboard sits beside the ZDX dashboards
pse-dashboard.detail: The earlier legacy statement was that a ZIA Private Service Edge dashboard exists separately from the standard ZDX dashboards and monitors on-prem edge health; the captured About ZDX Score article carries no related-articles list.
pse-dashboard.blocks: answers about where Virtual Service Edge health is monitored
pse-dashboard.resolution: Answered in part: the ZDX help documents a ZIA Private Service Edge Health dashboard, reached under Private Access > Dashboards > Health and supported on every subscription tier (claims pse-health, pse-tiles, pse-traffic, pse-datacenter and pse-instance in zdx.dashboards). Whether the Virtual Service Edge is covered is not stated, and the legacy claim that it is a separate view monitoring the on-prem edge was not checked beyond that.
